solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Serious man deemed wise around part of UK creates false god

indicators.note: around is read as 'in the vicinity of', so the wise man sits next to the region

parts.note: grave means serious or solemn
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom
a mage is a magician or learned sage

explanation.surface: A solemn sage is somehow responsible for producing an idol, near some corner of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' here means 'in the neighbourhood of', a positional link rather than a containment signal, so nothing goes inside anything.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol carved for worship, condemned in the Ten Commandments, is the biblical phrase for a false deity.

clue.text: Jamaican music or Indian music in which note is repeated

indicators.note: is repeated means the note appears a second time, added beside the one already in the word

parts.note: a raga is a melodic pattern in Indian classical music
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Jamaican or Indian music where one note recurs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dancehall style of reggae from Jamaica, so it names a Jamaican musical genre.

clue.text: Inappropriate verses priest originally used for evening prayer

indicators.note: inappropriate means out of place, so the letters are put in another order
originally means the first letter

explanation.surface: A priest was the first to use unsuitable verses at a nighttime service.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the service of evensong, held towards evening in church.

clue.text: Head is one inclined to get short-tempered, no leader

indicators.note: no leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a snapper is someone who snaps, speaking irritably

explanation.surface: The boss is an irritable type, but no leader.
explanation.definitionFit: This is old British slang for the head.

clue.text: Trading pioneer on offshore island, one hitting his targets?

parts.note: Michael Marks co-founded the British retailer Marks & Spencer
the Isle of Man lies off the British coast

explanation.surface: A retail pioneer living on an island meets his sales targets.
explanation.walkthrough: Marks & Spencer is a long-established British department store chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharpshooter is someone skilled at hitting a target, which the question mark punningly applies.

clue.text: Comedian to voice discontent, adding nothing

indicators.note: adding means the next piece is put on the end

parts.note: to grouch is to grumble
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A comic complains, but contributes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho Marx was the wisecracking American film comic of the Marx Brothers.

clue.text: Plant wrecks top of historic Welsh location — a piece of equipment being introduced

parts.note: mars means spoils or wrecks

indicators.note: top of means the first letter
being introduced means put inside, so these letters go into the town

parts.note: Mold is a town in north-east Wales
a rig is a piece of equipment, as in a drilling rig

explanation.surface: A plant spoils the summit of an old Welsh site as equipment is brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-flowered perennial grows in wet ground and is a specific plant species.

clue.text: Politician in London borough is piercing

indicators.note: in means the politician is placed within the borough

parts.note: Ealing is a borough of west London
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP in Ealing is sharp-tongued.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale something is to pierce it with a sharp stake, so the participle means piercing.

clue.text: It's right of king's eldest son maybe to be touring empire in trouble

definitions.text: It's right of king's eldest son maybe

indicators.note: in trouble means in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The heir's privilege is to tour an empire beset by unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the right of the firstborn son to inherit, as with a king's heir.

clue.text: Each returning soldier's protection

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for each is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier, with the possessive 's

explanation.surface: Every soldier coming home has some cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Under someone's aegis means under their sponsorship or shield, a synonym for protection.

clue.text: One doing something right, type to be embraced by fellow

indicators.note: being embraced by means being held inside, so the first pieces go within the fellow

parts.note: a peer is an equal or fellow
form means a type or kind

explanation.surface: Someone acting correctly gets hugged by a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor, musician or other entertainer is someone carrying out an act, a fair loose description.

clue.text: Lasses with hem that's ridiculous may be such?

definitions.text: Lasses with hem that's ridiculous may be such?

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurdly out of order, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Girls in absurdly short skirts might be thought brazen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works twice: the anagram of LASSES and HEM, and a picture of girls whose ridiculous hemlines show they lack modesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Girls wearing outrageous hemlines might be called brazen, without modesty or embarrassment.

clue.text: Opening piece of music has magnificence

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A concert's overture is grand and splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorge or deep gap in the ground is a wide opening.

clue.text: Soldiers trapped in mountain maybe — a dangerous situation

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside, so the soldiers go within the other piece

parts.note: a mountain is an example of a mass, a large heap
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops caught on a peak face peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog or quagmire is figuratively a mess or tangle that is hard to escape, a perilous position.

clue.text: In part of cell find bone, old and remarkable

parts.note: a rib is a bone
some can mean remarkable, as in 'that was some party'

explanation.surface: In a prison cell, someone finds an ancient, remarkable bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' suggests a prison; it is the biological cell.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tiny structure within a living cell where proteins are made, a cell component.

clue.text: Wheedling little woman Heather pursues retreating Bill

indicators.note: pursues means comes after, so heather is placed after the woman
retreating means going backwards, so the bill's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
Jo is one of the March sisters in Little Women
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: A small woman named Heather sweet-talks a man named Bill as he backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant LING. 'Little woman' points to Jo of Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaxing someone with flattery to get one's way is the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Vehicle with a king (merry one) making half-turn

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme was a merry old soul

explanation.surface: A cheerful king makes a half-turn in a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: In horsemanship, this is a half-turn to the right or left executed by a horse and rider.

clue.text: Hesitation about objection — speak briefly making counter-argument

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the hesitation is read backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: talk means speak

explanation.surface: Someone hesitating over a protest talks only briefly in reply to a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a refutation, the response that contradicts an opponent's case.

clue.text: Cane hurt once — sadly hard to forget

indicators.note: sadly means badly, so the letters are rearranged
to forget means to leave out, so the abbreviation for hard is removed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A caning hurt once, and sadly it is hard to forget.
explanation.definitionFit: To cane is to beat, and to thrash or defeat soundly is the same kind of beating.

clue.text: Military commander giving short demonstration with weapon

indicators.note: short means missing its last letter

parts.note: a show is a demonstration
a gun is a weapon

explanation.surface: A general puts on a brief display with his firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoguns were hereditary military rulers of feudal Japan.

clue.text: City dwelling without foundation not toppling over

indicators.note: without foundation means the bottom letter of a down entry is removed

parts.note: a house is a dwelling

indicators.note: toppling over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards in a down clue

explanation.surface: A city house lacking foundations still doesn't collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: This Texan metropolis is a large American city.

clue.text: Indication of pain, say, from little son getting yellowish-white

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
cream is a yellowish-white colour

explanation.surface: A child cries out after turning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud cry is an example of how someone signals they are hurt.

clue.text: Olympic Games time perhaps with no gold? Zero enjoyment!

indicators.note: with no means without, so the gold symbol is removed

parts.note: summer Olympics are often held in August
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: An athlete winning no gold at the Olympics finds no pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest or relish in doing something is the same as keen enjoyment.

clue.text: A superior monarch's palace in which a knight is well-informed

parts.note: U means upper class or superior

indicators.note: in which tells us the next pieces go inside the palace

parts.note: a court is a royal residence
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A grand royal residence houses a knight who knows everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means up to date, aware of the latest news.

clue.text: A sailor turning up, one with a lot on his shoulders

definitions.text: one with a lot on his shoulders

indicators.note: turning up means read upwards, backwards in a down clue

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor shows up, burdened with worries.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Titan bore the heavens on his shoulders, so he carries a great load.

clue.text: Fish may be lonesome swimming around lake

indicators.note: around means the scrambled word surrounds the lake
swimming suggests moving around fluidly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solitary fish swims around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a flatfish species prized for eating, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Rebel — audible one in action on the roof

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the word sounds like what goes in the grid

parts.words: one in action on the roof
parts.note: a tiler works on roofs

explanation.surface: A rebel makes himself heard while up on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat of that name led the Peasants' Revolt, so he is a famous example of an English insurgent.

clue.text: End-points covered by some Parisian master's original type of philosophy

indicators.note: covered by means placed inside, so the end-points go within the French word

parts.note: des is French for some
termini are the end-points of lines

indicators.note: original means the first letter

explanation.surface: A French master's founding idea of philosophy is circled by its end-points.
explanation.definitionFit: This doctrine holds that all events are fixed by prior causes, a school of philosophical thought.
